victim.value: Forrest Blake, elderly wealthy husband whose death is revealed to be suicide triggered by discovery of his wife's serial infidelities and betrayal by her young lover
victim.quote: Forrest had reached in his pocket and drawn out a heavy, baroque key which he fingered thoughtfully before Janet's stunned gaze.

culprit_and_motive.value: Janet Blake (indirectly responsible through moral culpability); Forrest Blake (direct agent of own death by suicide after discovering infidelity); the young lover acts as immediate catalyst by selling the apartment key to Forrest
culprit_and_motive.quote: It was the next morning she found him quite dead in his big bed, her first reaction was to laugh aloud in sheer relief.

resolution.value: Janet's own death by drowning at the pool, lured by Forrest's ghost, restores cosmic balance; the white moth motif (symbolizing lost souls) provides supernatural justice
resolution.quote: That is where they found her, face down at the bottom of the quiet pool.

investigator.value: Janet Blake herself; the reader experiences the mystery entirely through her perspective as she encounters Forrest's apparitions and gradually descends into guilt-driven madness
investigator.quote: Huddled in Forrest's big chair by the fireplace, her expertly maintained pale gold hair luminous against the dark leather, Janet reviewed the nightmare of the past weeks.
